turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Right. Blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven, temperature thirty-eight point three, and the weight is fifty-two kilograms.
[SEG0002] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Pulse is seventy-four. Last time in March you were sixty-eight. Your last pressure was one-forty. The doctor will be with you just now.
[SEG0003] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok, thanks. Umm, sorry I'm a bit all over the place, the robot near the garage was out and the bakkie was just sitting there.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ag, no worries, you're here now. So tell me, what's the trouble?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): It's my elbow. The outside of the right one has been really sore.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ok, the outer side. How long has it been, and what sets it off?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, six weeks. Well actually I thought maybe a month, no, it's six weeks. Lifting a cup of tea is, eish, sharp now, and gripping the brush at work is worse.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. Any swelling, redness, or does it feel hot?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No swelling, it's not red, and it doesn't feel hot.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pins and needles, or tingling in the fingers?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. The hand is fine.

[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Of. I'm already thinking of that tendon on the outside that takes the load when you grip, but let me not jump. Tell me the work, the hours, what you eat, exercise, and if you drink.

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, I'm a painter, houses mostly, sometimes a bit of carpentry if the site needs it, umm six days a week from about seven until four, later if the client is pushing. Diet is mostly pap and veg and a lot of coffee from the flask. I don't really exercise besides the work itself. And I have a beer or two on a Friday, not during the week.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Family side, any sugar or blood pressure or joint problems?

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, my father had diabetes in his fifties, my mother did not, my older sister is fine as far as I know, and another sister has pressure but no sugar. Nobody in the family had this elbow thing, hey.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): And medicines, what are you actually taking for this?

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): I take ibuprophen, the four hundred milligram tablets, by mouth, twice a day with food, for the elbow. Is that going to burn a hole in my stomach? I've been worrying about that the whole time.

[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): With food, at that dose, for a few weeks, I think that's reasonable. Your temperature was thirty-eight point three, which is a bit up, so I'm just thinking out loud whether you're brewing something. Have you felt feverish or shivery?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I don't feel feverish, no shivers. But is thirty-eight point three dangerous, like is the elbow infected? I googled it and now I can't sleep.

[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): I don't think it's an infection, the story doesn't fit a septic joint. There's a sharp tender spot on the outer bump of the right elbow, no warmth in the joint, and I can't see any swelling. Push your wrist up against my hand. Ja, that brings the same pain on.

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Ow, ja, that's the spot. Umm, actually, wait, I said there was no tingling, but when I've been gripping the brush all day there is tingling down the forearm into the hand. I forgot, sorry.

[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Err, that actually helps me. Tingling after a long grip still fits the elbow, not a nerve pinched in the neck. My working impression is lateral epicondylitis, tennis elbow, from the repetitive painting.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it arthritis? Am I going to need an operation? And can I still paint, because if I drop the jobs there's no pay, you know how it is.

[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not arthritis, hey, the joint itself moves nicely, and I'm not thinking of an operation at all. You can keep painting, but ease the heavy gripping and use the other hand for the kettle, so the tendon gets a chance.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. What about a brace, someone on site said a strap? And physio, does that actually work? How long is this going to go on for?

[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): A counterforce brace, the strap sitting just below the sore spot, helps a lot of painters. I'll refer you to physio and they'll book you from the front desk. I'd like about six weeks of that before we add anything else.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): And an injection? My cousin had one in the shoulder and she said it was awful. Are you going to inject me today?
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): No injection today. If it has not settled after the physio, we might do a steroid injection then, but not now. Come back and see me in six weeks either way.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Six weeks, shame. Where do I get the strap, the chemist by the garage? And should I ice it, or is heat better?

[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): The chemist is fine, any counterforce elbow strap. Ice it for ten minutes after work, not heat, and don't stretch it aggressively. If it turns properly hot, red, and you feel ill, don't wait the six weeks, come in sooner.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. And the tingling, you're not worried it's a stroke or something? I know that sounds silly, I've just been anxious the whole week.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not a stroke. Tingling from the elbow after gripping is a local tendon thing, not the brain. See you in six weeks, and the physio note will be at reception.

spec.situation: Painter or carpenter with outer elbow pain for six weeks, worse lifting a cup; takes ibuprofen; physio and brace advice; no injection yet.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

bad.reason: Doctor says current dose with food for a few weeks is reasonable, but doesn't explicitly recommend continuing.
bad.text: Continue ibuprofen 400 mg by mouth twice a day with food for a few weeks (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)

omissions.text: Physical exam finding: the right elbow joint itself moves nicely / range of motion preserved.
Negative finding/exam: doctor said this does not fit a septic joint / he does not think the elbow is infected.
Plan detail: no operation is being considered.
Plan detail: physiotherapy should be tried for about six weeks before adding anything else.
Follow-up/plan detail: physiotherapy note will be at reception and front desk will book physiotherapy.
Negative finding: doctor reassured that the tingling is not from a pinched nerve in the neck.
Negative finding/reassurance: doctor said the tingling is not a stroke / not from the brain.
Recorded symptom is overstated: difficulty sleeping was attributed to worry after googling possible infection, not documented as an independent neurological symptom.
